title: Why Did This 720-Ton Titan Sing at Dawn? 🌅
hook_sentence: In 27 BC, a major earthquake shattered the northern colossus, collapsing the statue from the waist up and cracking its lower half.
narration_script: In 27 BC, a major earthquake shattered the northern colossus, collapsing the statue from the waist up and cracking its lower half. Following the earthquake damage, the northern monument became famous throughout the ancient world for emitting a reported cry at dawn. Reaching a total height of 60 feet (18 m) including their 13-foot (4 m) pedestals, each colossus weighs an estimated 720 tons. The last reliable historical record of the statue vocalizing dates to the year 196 AD. Local tradition dates the reconstruction of the statue's upper tiers to around 199 AD. Still, the colossi have stood since 1350 BC, originally carved to guard the memorial temple where Amenhotep III was worshipped.
closing_sentence: Still, the colossi have stood since 1350 BC, originally carved to guard the memorial temple where Amenhotep III was worshipped.
caption:
For centuries, travelers gathered at dawn across Egypt's Theban Necropolis to witness stone make a sound. 🌅

In November 130 AD, the poet Julia Balbilla inscribed poetry on the colossus commemorating multiple hearings of the sound during an imperial visit with Emperor Hadrian. Local tradition dates the reconstruction of the statue's upper tiers to around 199 AD, attributing the repair to Roman Emperor Septimius Severus. By one estimate, the base of the vocal colossus preserves approximately 90 surviving traveler inscriptions testifying whether or not the visitor heard the sound.

Would you travel across an empire just to hear a shattered stone speak at dawn? 🏛️
